To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ratio of K(+)/K(-) APP mRNA isoforms increases in the brains of patients with Alzheimer's disease.

(1) KPI(+) APP mRNA isoforms are significantly upregulated in the cerebral cortex of AD brains; (2) KPI(-) APP mRNA isoforms remain unchanged; and (3) the ratio KPI(+) / KPI(-) increases in AD brains.
the ratio of Kunitz protease inhibitor containing APP mRNA to KPI(-), APP(751) mRNA increases in Alzheimer's disease cerebral cortex.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression of mRNA isoform levels of APP and their relationship to the pathology of AD.
the role of APP mRNA in the aetiology of Alzheimer's disease.
the role of protease inhibitors on the processing of the amyloid precursor protein in Alzheimer's disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the KPI(751), KPI(770), APR(365) and KPI(563) isoforms of the APP gene are up-regulated in the AD brain.
there is a significant increase in the KPI(+/KPI-APP) ratio in AD brains relative controls.
APP KPI(+) isoforms are increased specifically in AD cerebral cortex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the KPI(+/-) ratio of APP isoforms is increased in AD brains and this may be due to a change in the expression of the APP gene.
the KPI(+), APP mRNA levels are increased in Alzheimer's disease brains.
APP mRNA isoforms containing the KPI domain are increased in the cerebral cortex of AD brains.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the increase in APP mRNA levels was not due to an increase in the APP695 isoform, but rather an increase in APP isoforms containing the KPI domain.
there are changes in the levels of mRNA for the protease inhibitor isoforms of APP in AD.
there was a change in the mRNA isoforms expressed in the AD brain.
